text:
The Sharks look like a team whose future showed up early. Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith and Ivar Stenberg have been in 79 headlines between them in two weeks, and the line has earned them: Smith's three-point night against Nashville was called one of the best NHL games of the year in one headline, and Stenberg has moved into the top six beside them since Igor Chernyshov went on injured reserve. It isn't all sunshine. Coach Ryan Warsofsky is healthy-scratching Collin Graf and Michael Kesselring tonight, and the beat says the message is to be harder to play against.

The numbers explain why. San Jose has 45% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of the chances) and its penalty kill allows 0.96 expected goals a game. A 3-1-1 run lifted them a point ahead of Seattle in the Pacific, but our numbers keep their playoff chance at 7%. Alex Nedeljkovic starts over Yaroslav Askarov, and he has been good: 6.8 goals saved above expected in eight games.

Seattle arrives off its best night in a while, a 5-1 win over Vancouver that snapped a three-game slide and featured a Berkly Catton hat trick. Catton has 11 points in his last ten games in his second season, though our numbers say finishing is doing most of that work. The Kraken are without Jared McCann until January, and Kaapo Kakko has moved beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich, and that line was humming against Vancouver. Their record (21 points) is well ahead of their chances (17.2 expected points), with 45% of the five-on-five share. Philipp Grubauer starts.

Two young teams at the same share, one point apart in the division. Our numbers lean San Jose, 3.27 expected goals to 2.93. Celebrini is at 82% for a point, and Michael Misa and Stenberg are our sleepers.
headline: The Sharks' kids, and a Catton hat trick
